newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols soften as spot holds 115.00.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dlr/yen vols soften as spot holds 115.00.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/yen options edged lower in quiet U.S. trading as the day progressed and the spot recovered from an overnight dip below 115.00 yen.
"The real action in dollar/yen has been in the Tokyo session," said a U.S. trader for a European bank.
The dollar was bid at 115.70 yen at midafternoon after slipping to 114.90 in Asia overnight on a jump in Japan's April trade surplus.
Currency traders said an abundance of sellers on the way back up put the brakes on the uptick in spot dollar/yen and capped volatility.
Late in the trading session, implied volatility was 11.7/12.0 percent for one-month dollar/yen options, down from 12.1/12.4 percent at the New York open and virtually unchanged from Friday.
A decisive break below 115.00 yen could send volatilities higher again, unless interest in options strikes from 112.00 to 115.00 has been spent over the past few weeks, the European bank trader said.
The one-month 25-delta risk reversal also was basically steady at 1.1/1.4 in favor of yen calls, reflecting the continued strong bias for the calls after the dollar shed more than 12 yen this month.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin addresses the Japan Society's annual dinner in New York this evening, and currency market participants said they would monitor his remarks especially closely in light of the strong Japanese trade data and the dollar's recent sharp drop.

The session's subdued activity reflected hesitancy to establish positions before Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee and a holiday across much of Europe, traders said. A Reuters poll found 21 of 39 primary dealers expect U.S. central bankers to leave interest rates unchanged at the meeting.
One-month dollar/mark volatility was steady at 9.1/9.4 percent, with risk reversals still marginally skewed to mark calls at 0.1/0.4.
